articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026.
This amendment updates previous guidance concerning transactions related to Iran, though specific details of the changes were not immediately released.
Such amendments typically aim to clarify existing authorizations, introduce new permissible activities, or adjust restrictions within the Iran sanctions program.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entity for North Korea IT Worker Schemes and DRC-Related Activities
body: On October 28, 2026, OFAC announced new designations targeting individuals and one entity involved in North Korean government-run IT worker schemes that defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for the DPRK's weapons programs.
The action specifically targeted 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in these illicit activities.
Additionally, OFAC announced designations related to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, though specific details on these designations were not immediately available.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Chainalysis / NK News

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle nine apparent violations of Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme exported networking equipment and related services from the United States to a Russian defense manufacturer, Joint Stock Company Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA).
MMZA was blocked by operation of law due to its majority ownership by the designated JSC Concern Almaz-Antey. OFAC determined the violations were egregious and voluntarily self-disclosed.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Corruption, Crime & Compliance

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Reporting Obligations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced multiple amendments to its Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports.

These revisions, part of an ongoing review of published sanctions guidance, address financial institutions' obligations when processing transactions involving sanctioned parties, maintaining blocked accounts, and submitting regulatory reports.
Key updates clarify the distinction between blocking and rejecting transactions, the treatment of blocked funds, and reporting requirements through the OFAC Reporting System (ORS).
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / KPMG / Sanctions Expert Feed

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related and Russia-Related General Licenses, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: On October 21, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses, alongside the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea.
The issuance of new General Licenses typically authorizes specific transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under existing sanctions programs.
The removal of designations indicates a change in the sanctioned status of certain individuals or entities, potentially easing restrictions on them.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Designations and General Licenses Under Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA)
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations and associated General Licenses under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026.
These actions aim to combat the theft and misappropriation of American intellectual property, a critical component of U.S. national security and economic prosperity.
The accompanying General Licenses are intended to provide clarity and authorization for certain transactions that may be impacted by these new designations.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License for Earthquake Relief Efforts
body: On October 16, 2026, OFAC issued Venezuela-related General License (GL) 60A, which amends and supersedes GL 60.

This amended General License authorizes transactions related to earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela, extending the authorization period from its original end date of October 23, 2026, to April 21, 2027.
Venezuela-related FAQ 1263 was also amended to reflect this extended authorization.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals Related to Iran and Cuba, Issues New General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related and Cuba designations on October 15, 2026.
These designations target individuals and entities deemed to be involved in activities contrary to U.S. foreign policy and national security interests concerning Iran and Cuba.
In conjunction with these designations, OFAC also issued new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions to provide guidance on permissible activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Jorge Rodriguez from Venezuela Sanctions List
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) removed Jorge Rodriguez, the head of Venezuela's National Assembly, from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list on October 14, 2026.
This delisting ends the associated asset freeze and removes obstacles for U.S. persons attempting to deal with him.
Rodriguez, who has served as President of Venezuela's National Assembly since 2021, was initially designated in 2018.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Al Jazeera / Steptoe

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: On October 13, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These designations aim to disrupt the financial networks and operations of those engaged in illicit drug trafficking and terrorist financing globally.
The specific individuals and entities designated were not immediately detailed in the initial announcement but are subject to asset freezes and other restrictions.

articles.headline: EU Designates Individuals and Entities for Sanctions Circumvention and Illicit Trade with Russia
body: The Council of the European Union adopted additional restrictive measures against three individuals and nine entities on October 15, 2026.
These designations target those involved in the import of sanctioned goods to Russia and the circumvention of EU sanctions related to oil and financial transactions.
The listed individuals and entities are subject to an asset freeze, a prohibition on making funds or economic resources available, and a travel ban for natural persons.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Fined $1,529,685 by OFAC for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc. has agreed to pay a civil penalty of $1,529,685 to the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

The settlement resolves nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations, stemming from the export of networking equipment and services to a blocked Russian defense manufacturer.
The violations were deemed egregious and voluntarily self-disclosed by Extreme Networks.

articles.headline: Bank of America Settles with OFAC for $11,662,930 Over Multiple Sanctions Violations
body: Bank of America, N.A. has agreed to an $11,662,930 settlement with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).
The settlement resolves 475 apparent violations of various OFAC sanctions programs, including those targeting Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

The apparent violations involved processing payments through blocked banks, failing to prioritize alerts for sanctioned customers, not promptly updating watchlists, and mishandling accounts associated with blocked persons.

articles.headline: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics Fined $175,015 by OFAC for Counter Narcotics Sanctions Violations
body: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, a California-based freight forwarder, has agreed to pay $175,015 to settle apparent violations of OFAC counter narcotics sanctions and reporting obligations.

The violations occurred when Pegasus arranged the shipment of equipment from a designated Chinese supplier, Youli Technology Development Co., Ltd., and failed to identify it as such due to compliance program deficiencies.
OFAC also cited Pegasus for initially failing to respond fully to an administrative subpoena, highlighting the importance of thorough inquiry and accurate responses to information requests.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Corruption, Crime & Compliance / Ferrari & Associates

articles.headline: Adani Enterprises Limited Settles with OFAC for $275 Million Over Iran Sanctions Violations
body: Adani Enterprises Limited (AEL), a diversified multinational company headquartered in India, has agreed to pay $275,000,000 to settle its potential civil liability for apparent violations of OFAC sanctions on Iran.

From November 2023 to June 2025, AEL purchased shipments of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) from a Dubai-based trader, causing U.S. financial institutions to process 32 U.S. dollar-denominated payments totaling approximately $192 million.
Red flags should have indicated that the LPG actually originated from Iran, and OFAC deemed the violations egregious and not voluntarily self-disclosed.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Akrivis Law Group, PLLC / Comsure, Jersey

articles.headline: FTI Consulting, Inc. Fined $1,050,000 by OFAC for Russia-Related Sanctions Violations
body: FTI Consulting, Inc., a Washington, D.C.-based global advisory firm, has agreed to pay $1,050,000 to settle with OFAC.
The settlement addresses apparent violations related to indirectly dealing in the prohibited debt of VTB Bank OAO, an entity on OFAC's Sectoral Sanctions Identification (SSI) List.
The violations involved issuing invoices whose ultimate obligor was VTB and continuing work even as those invoices went unpaid beyond the permissible tenor.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Akrivis Law Group, PLLC

articles.headline: OCC Announces October 2026 Enforcement Actions, Including Penalties for BSA/AML Deficiencies
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released its enforcement actions for October 2026, detailing various penalties against financial institutions and individuals.

Among the actions, the OCC issued a Cease and Desist Order and a Civil Money Penalty against American Express National Bank for deficiencies in its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance program, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports, and customer due diligence violations.

The OCC also imposed a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, National Association, for similar BSA compliance program deficiencies, failure to file suspicious activity reports, and inaccurate transmittor name information in wire transfers.

Jennifer Hamblin, a Vault Teller at a Cincinnati, Ohio, branch of Fifth Third Bank, N.A., was prohibited from banking affairs for embezzling approximately $292,000 in customer funds.

Similarly, Christopher Organista, a Former Operations Processor at U.S. Bank National Association in La Mirada, California, received a prohibition order for embezzling approximately $194,131 in bank customer funds.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
